name: Baton
why: sterile monochrome product proof; publisher identity incorrectly imposed on the fictional subject. (Ledger also: thin neutral monochrome UI that disappears at social-feed scale; "The final result was internally tidy but emotionally flat and too easy to transplant to another startup.")
note: Folder kept as negative evidence; do not use in a positive reference set. Source calls the feedback 'direct rejection evidence' from the user; which founder is not recorded. Exercise window 2026-08-29 to 2026-08-30. Also context: 01-recent-concept-lessons.md 'What Baton exposed' (mobile + extra QA done though only a desktop X screenshot was requested).

name: Linecheck
why: user rejected the overall hero. The industrial photograph, giant headline and right-side inspection panel still formed a familiar template despite the product-specific details. (Assessment: oversized neutral-grotesk headline; copy and CTA isolated in a conventional marketing block; generated industrial photograph as the dominant shortcut; a single application panel placed over the image; familiar blue CTA and arrow treatment.)
note: ASSESSMENT.md: 'Status: rejected by the user on 2026-08-30. Do not use this concept as a positive benchmark.' Second source file: inbox/linecheck-hero-proof-2026-08-30/ASSESSMENT.md. It improved the subject/publisher boundary and used coherent sample data but the skeleton was the problem.

name: Take
why: materially better received than Baton and Linecheck. Useful lesson is not the exact layout but that the whole frame belongs to a product world: brand field, material, interface vocabulary, image, type and action reinforce one premise. (Concept notes: concrete product, collaborative video review; timecode, annotation and media review as visual language; one decisive brand field and a cinematic product stage; legible nav, unmistakable main action.)
note: RELATIVE accept ('materially better received', 'positive evidence'), not an unqualified approval; ledger says future work must exceed it, and it is not a template. No html in the KB, only the final render. Visual: near-black field with acid lime, which the team's own AI-cluster list treats as a tell in general; accepted because of subject fit. Original concept lessons: 01-recent-concept-lessons.md.

name: Mise
why: materially better received than Baton and Linecheck. Useful lesson is not the exact layout but that the whole frame belongs to a product world. (Concept notes: domain with physical evidence, production planning for food teams; palette, imagery and interface content derived from ingredients, batches and kitchen operations; one image and one operational layer carry the composition; different identity from Take at the same quality bar.)
note: RELATIVE accept, same caveats as Take. No html in the KB, only final render.

name: Borne
why: accepted as good. Useful signals: calm full-bleed photography, restrained navigation, refined serif typography, quiet booking control and a coherent premium atmosphere.
note: Positive evidence, not a template; preserve restraint and spatial confidence without repeating the exact skeleton. Captured from direct user feedback on 2026-08-30. Part of the 'hero collection R1'; no source files for Borne exist in the KB.

name: Nacre
why: accepted as good. Useful signals: sculptural central product, spacious composition, restrained palette, elegant display typography and information placed around the image rather than inside a generic content block.
note: Positive evidence, not a template. No source files in the KB.

name: Caption: plain description of the work (e.g. 'hero section concept')
why: Plain description is the default caption. Rokas, 2026-08-31, after rejecting two agent drafts. Something like "simple hero section page with vibrant colors" is the register: say what the thing is, add nothing, let the image carry it.
note: Founder caption rule recorded in my-thinking.md ('Rokas, 2026-08-31'); related synthesis in inbox/x-post-descriptions-2026-08-30/SYNTHESIS.md. Caption-pattern verdict, not a design concept.

name: Caption naming the fictional brand (Finlyti-style 'Name - category template')
why: Never put the fictional brand's name in the caption. Rokas, 2026-08-31, stated as a rule: the brand does not exist, so its name carries nothing for a reader; overrides post-13's format even though it scored 13.5x reach.
note: Founder caption rule recorded in my-thinking.md ('Rokas, 2026-08-31'); related synthesis in inbox/x-post-descriptions-2026-08-30/SYNTHESIS.md. Caption-pattern verdict, not a design concept.

name: Caption written from inside the fiction (ad for the fake company)
why: Do not write the caption from inside the fiction. A concept post is not an ad for the fake company. "i made the meeting bot knock before it joins" sells a feature of a company that does not exist.
